claim: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for multiple chronic diseases, including cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and cancer.
source: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for multiple chronic diseases, including cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and cancer (Gallagher and LeRoith, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: According to the WHO, obesity is defined as 'abnormal or excessive fat accumulation that presents a risk to health'.
source: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), obesity is defined as 'abnormal or excessive fat accumulation that presents a risk to health' (World Health Organization, 2000).
evidence: This is a definition from the WHO, cited in the manuscript.

claim: Body mass index (BMI) is the most appropriate measure for overweight and obesity because the cut-offs account for age, sex, and ethnicity.
source: Body mass index (BMI) is the most appropriate measure for overweight and obesity because the cut-offs account for age, sex, and ethnicity (World Health Organization, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to WHO guidelines.

claim: Obesity has increased substantially in many settings, including in Hong Kong.
source: Obesity has increased substantially in many settings, including in Hong Kong.
evidence: This is a general statement about obesity trends.

claim: Obesity is complicated with multifactorial risk factors, such as socioeconomic position (SEP), mood disturbance, and genetic factors.
source: Obesity is complicated with multifactorial risk factors, such as socioeconomic position (SEP), mood disturbance, and genetic factors (Cardel et al., 2020), so there is a need to evaluate their roles in obesity comprehensively and systematically (Manrai et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Most studies on targets of obesity are conducted in a western setting.
source: Moreover, given most studies on targets of obesity are conducted in a western setting (Cardel et al., 2020), a comprehensive assessment of modifiable factors of early life obesity in a non-western setting, with a different social structure, provides a valuable opportunity to identify novel exposures.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Environment-wide association studies (EWAS) enable assessment of a variety of exposures across the human environmental exposome in a high-throughput manner.
source: Environment-wide association studies (EWAS) enable us to assess a variety of exposures across the human environmental exposome in a high-throughput manner (Hall et al., 2013), similar to genome-wide association studies for genetic associations.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Previous EWAS have been performed on outcomes, such as type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and childhood obesity in western settings but not in a Chinese setting.
source: Previous EWAS have been performed on outcomes, such as type 2 diabetes (Patel et al., 2010), cardiovascular disease (Zhuang et al., 2018), and childhood obesity in western settings (Vrijheid et al., 2020; Uche et al., 2020) but not in a Chinese setting.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In previous EWAS of childhood obesity in the US (6–17 years old), UK, and Europe (6–11 years old), second-hand smoking was related to higher childhood BMI.
source: In the previous EWAS of childhood obesity in the US (6–17 years old), UK, and Europe (6–11 years old), second-hand smoking was related to higher childhood BMI, whilst some other exposures, such as vitamins, were not consistently associated with obesity in these settings (Vrijheid et al., 2020; Uche et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published EWAS studies.

claim: DNA methylation may modulate gene expression and thereby influence susceptibility to obesity or obesity-related chronic disease.
source: DNA methylation may modulate gene expression and thereby influence susceptibility to obesity or obesity-related chronic disease (Fall et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: DNA methylation at cg06500161 was previously identified as related to obesity in the US.
source: For example, DNA methylation at cg06500161 was previously identified as related to obesity in the US (Huang et al., 2018a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a published epigenome-wide association study.

claim: Unlike genetic variants, DNA methylation is modifiable and may change in response to environmental factors or disease.
source: Unlike genetic variants, DNA methylation is modifiable and may change in response to environmental factors or disease and therefore might be open to confounding by these factors (Fall et al., 2017; Fraga et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Most Chinese people in Hong Kong are first-, second-, or third-generation migrants from the neighbouring province of Guangdong in southern China.
source: Most Chinese people in Hong Kong are first-, second-, or third-generation migrants from the neighbouring province of Guangdong in southern China.
evidence: This is a demographic fact about Hong Kong's population.

claim: Dietary habits of people in Hong Kong are similar to those in southern China, although also influenced by western culture.
source: Dietary habits of people in Hong Kong are similar to those in southern China, although also influenced by western culture (Leung et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Active smoking among Chinese mothers was rare while maternal exposure to second-hand smoking during pregnancy was common before the smoking ban in public and workplaces was implemented in 2007.
source: Lifestyle in Hong Kong also differs from more commonly studied western populations on some important attributes, for example, active smoking among Chinese mothers was rare while maternal exposure to second-hand smoking during pregnancy was common before the smoking ban in public and workplaces was implemented in 2007 (Lee, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The 'Children of 1997' birth cohort is a large (n = 8327) population-representative Chinese cohort in Hong Kong.
source: The study takes advantage of the 'Children of 1997' birth cohort, a large (n = 8327) population-representative Chinese cohort in Hong Kong (Schooling et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a description of the cohort used in the study, supported by a citation.

claim: The participants were originally recruited shortly after birth in April and May 1997 at all of the 49 Maternal and Child Health Centers (MCHCs) in Hong Kong.
source: The participants were originally recruited shortly after birth in April and May 1997 at all of the 49 Maternal and Child Health Centers (MCHCs) in Hong Kong, which provide free check-ups and immunizations.
evidence: This describes the recruitment process for the cohort.

claim: The study included 88% of births in the relevant period.
source: The study included 88% of births in the relevant period.
evidence: This describes the coverage of the cohort.

claim: At ~11.5 years, BMI was calculated from height and weight measurements records provided by the Student Health Service, the Department of Health.
source: At ~11.5 years, BMI was calculated from height and weight measurements records provided by the Student Health Service, the Department of Health.
evidence: This describes the data source for BMI measurements at ~11.5 years.

claim: Waist–hip ratio (WHR) was calculated based on waist and hip circumference collected in Survey I conducted in 2008–2009.
source: Waist–hip ratio (WHR) was calculated based on waist and hip circumference collected in Survey I conducted in 2008–2009.
evidence: This describes the data source for WHR measurements.

claim: At ~17.6 years, BMI was assessed by bio-electrical impedance analysis (BIA) with a Tanita segmental body composition monitor.
source: At ~17.6 years, in both phases of the Biobank Clinical follow-up, BMI was assessed by bio-electrical impedance analysis (BIA) with a Tanita segmental body composition monitor (Tanita BC-545, Tanita Co, Tokyo, Japan).
evidence: This describes the method for BMI assessment at ~17.6 years.

claim: Obesity was classified as BMI ≥20.89 kg/m2 for boys and BMI ≥21.20 kg/m2 for girls at age 11.5.
source: Given BMI has a more accepted cut-off value than WHR for children, we classified obesity as BMI ≥20.89 kg/m2 for boys and BMI ≥21.20 kg/m2 for girls at age 11.5; and BMI ≥24.73 kg/m2 for men and BMI ≥24.85 kg/m2 for women at age 17.6 (Cole et al., 2000).
evidence: This describes the obesity classification criteria used in the study, supported by a citation.

claim: Obesity was classified as BMI ≥24.73 kg/m2 for men and BMI ≥24.85 kg/m2 for women at age 17.6.

claim: After excluding exposures with missing values ≥50%, 123 exposures for BMI and 115 exposures for WHR at ~11.5 years were included.
source: After excluding exposures with missing values ≥50%, we included 123 exposures for BMI and 115 exposures for WHR at ~11.5 years, and 441 exposures for BMI and WHR at ~17.6 years using information from the original study, record linkage, the three surveys, that is Survey I (2008–2009), Survey II (2010–2012), and Survey III (2011–2012), as well as the Biobank Clinical follow-up.
